in_hebrew.name: יונה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יונה הוא שמו של דגל שהגיע מיוון וסמלו של הנאמנות, שבועת הנאמנות, והוא נקשר לדמותו של יונה הנביא, שהצליח לשכנע את העיר נינוה להתנצל ולהתחנן, שבעקבות זאת, הועברה עליה גזירה נוספה. השם הפך לסמל נאמנות, עצמאות ותמיכה, והוא חשוב בחברות נוצריות ובעיקר בבריטניה, שם הוא נחשב לאחד השמות הפופולריים ביותר.

in_greek.name: Ἰουνώ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἰουνώ היה שמו של דגל שהגיע מיוון וסמלו של הנאמנות, שבועת הנאמנות, והוא נקשר לדמותו של Ἰωνᾶς, שהצליח לשכנע את העיר Νίνευה להתנצל ולהתחנן, שבעקבות זאת, הועברה עליה γέγραπται נוספה. השם Ἰουνώ הפך לסמל νἱκη, ἀνεψιά, και ἔλεος, והוא חשוב בἐκκλησία ἐκκλησιαστική και νἱκη.

in_english.name: Juno
in_english.meaning: symbol of devotion, loyalty, and commitment, also associated with the biblical figure of Jonah
in_english.long_meaning: Juno, a name of Greek origin, symbolizing devotion, loyalty, and commitment. It is associated with the biblical figure of Jonah, who successfully convinced the city of Nineveh to repent and seek forgiveness. The name Juno became a symbol of devotion, faithfulness, and commitment, and is an important name in Christian cultures, particularly in Britain, where it is one of the most popular names. In Christian tradition, Juno represents the values of faithfulness, obedience, and devotion to God.

biblical_reference.note: The story of Jonah and the people of Nineveh is a well-known biblical account of repentance and forgiveness.

data.cultural_impact: Juno was the patron goddess of ancient Rome, and her worship spread with the Roman Empire's expansion. She was believed to be the protector of Rome and its people. Roman brides wore veils, derived from Juno's veil, during wedding ceremonies to ensure her protection. Juno's festival, the Junalia, was celebrated annually in honor of her protection, fertility, and childbirth. Her temple, the Temple of Juno Moneta, was the Roman mint and was believed to protect Rome's financial stability.
data.spiritual_significance: For ancient Romans, Juno represented the ultimate mother figure. She was the goddess of marriage, and her protection assured the successful continuation of the family unit. She was also believed to be the protector of childbirth and mothers. In spiritual terms, Juno symbolizes the divine protector and the ultimate mother figure, giving strength, support, and protection. Her presence ensures the success and continuation of families, relationships, and communities.

historical_references.reference: Juno was the Roman goddess of marriage, childbirth, and the protection of the Roman state. She was identified with the Greek Hera and the Etruscan Nelly.
Juno Lucina was a Roman goddess, who was believed to preside over childbirth. She was often identified with the Greek goddess Hera-Lakasma and the Etruscan goddess Uni.
